mechanics.name: Resurgence
mechanics.currentEffect: After you are unhooked by any means, Resurgence instantly grants you healing progression equal to 50/60/70% of a full health state, according to perk tier.
activation: Be unhooked by any means, including an unhook performed by yourself.
Ends/deactivates when: The granted healing progression is applied immediately; no continuing effect remains.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.1.0): Increased healing progression granted to 50/60/70% from 40/45/50%.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Being unhooked instantly fills 50/60/70% of your healing progress, depending on perk tier.
mechanics.oncePerTrialOrOtherLimits: Triggers on each time you are unhooked; no once-per-Trial limit is specified.
specialInteractions: The granted amount is healing progression, not a healing-speed bonus.

editorial.summary: Every unhook instantly gives you 50/60/70% of a full heal worth of progress.
useCases: Punish Killers who leave hook after securing pressure elsewhere.
Reduce the time two Survivors spend healing instead of repairing generators.
counters: Haemorrhage can erase stored healing progress if you are not healed quickly.
A Killer who immediately tunnels may deny the reset window.
Broken prevents completing the heal until it ends.
pros: Saves both your time and the healer’s time.
cons: Does nothing before your first unhook.
Healing progress can be lost to Haemorrhage.
Less valuable if you intentionally stay injured.
analysis: Resurgence looks simple because it is simple, and that is exactly why it ranks so highly. A Tier III proc begins the post-unhook heal at 70%, turning what would normally be a substantial two-player reset into a very short interaction. That time saving compounds because two Survivors are freed to repair, rescue, or reposition earlier.

Unlike many strong perks, Resurgence does not ask for a difficult trigger, map condition, or teammate communication. Getting unhooked is a normal match event. The perk converts that unavoidable event into reliable tempo, making it one of the cleanest examples of a high-floor perk with genuine top-end strength.

The biggest practical counter is Haemorrhage. If the team hesitates after the unhook, the stored progress can bleed away. The second is direct tunneling, where there may be no safe opportunity to finish the heal. That is why Resurgence pairs so naturally with anti-tunnel perks: one protects your reset window while the other makes the reset almost instantaneous.

In Solo Q, its predictability is gold because random teammates only need to recognize that you are nearly healed. In SWF, the team can deliberately plan short resets around it. For players choosing unlocks, Jill offers one of the most universally useful perks in the game.
editorial.verdict: An elite time-efficiency perk. If you are normally healed after unhooks, Resurgence turns one of the match’s most common downtime moments into a tiny speed bump.
